notes.title: Great moments in PC gaming: The 'ludicrous gibs' of Rise of the Triad
notes.notes:
Great moments in PC gaming are short, bite-sized celebrations of some of our favorite gaming memories. 

The 1990s were a good time for videogame gore. If you really wanted to see some spinal cords being removed, games had you covered. Two year after Mortal Kombat and one year after Doom, Rise of the Triad was a particularly memorable example of the artform that is making red stuff coming out of people in entertaining ways.

Apogee had been working on a sequel to Wolfenstein 3D when the project was canceled, leaving them with a bunch of first-person shooter assets. They built Rise of the Triad on those bones (and it was later renamed Rise of the Triad: Dark War to differentiate it from the remake). Apogee improved on Wolfenstein in a bunch of ways, especially with the scale of their game's destructibility. Glass shattered, bulletholes persisted, and various bits of level scenery like plants and lights broke. 

The most impressive destruction was that visited on the enemies, who popped into red smears. Hit them with a rocket and they were reduced to spinning offal: an eyeball; a severed hand that gave the finger as it passed; a skull with some of that attached spinal cord the '90s was all about. Accompanying this carnage was the message "Ludicrous Gibs!" because 'gibs' was apparently short for giblets at Apogee. This bit of internal studio slang would go on to be referenced by Quake and become a lasting bit of videogame lore. 

It may not seem like much today, but the first time an eyeball slid down your screen it was pretty special. What a time to be alive.

notes.title: Rise of the Triad soundtrack hits iTunes and elsewhere today
notes.notes:
The Rise of the Triad announcement teased last week has been revealed, and it's not a sequel: It's a soundtrack! And no, that's not quite as exciting as a new game, but Dave Oshry, Rise of the Triad's principal director and marketing dude, says there's more to come in the future.

"We've got a list of things we want to do, things we're working on and things that may or may not happen," he said. "I don't want to promise anything (because that's never a good idea in game development) but we're 100 percent committed to continuing to add features, content, tweaks and value to the ROTT reboot this year and continuing to reward the people who pre-ordered the game or were there playing with us on day one."

Longer term, he said the studio is aiming to release a "Ludicrous Edition" of the game that will collect everything—the Rise of the Triad remake, the soundtrack, the original 1995 release, the Extreme ROTT map pack, and whatever else it comes up with—into a single package. "And want to give that to people who pre-ordered the game for free, as a reward for being part of the ROTT community," Oshry said. "They've been getting weird with us for two years now and some of them have been fans of all things ROTT for 20 years now. It's a fun IP to be a part of."

As for the soundtrack, it contains 30 tracks composed by Andrew Hulshult, with inspirational titles like "Suck This," "Run Like Smeg," "I Choose the Stairs," "M-M-M-Menu," and, "OWW." Only about 20 of the tracks are actually in Rise of the Triad, but all of them will be remastered and added to the game in a future update. It's available now on Steam and will arrive soon on iTunes, Google Play, Spotify, and other fine purveyors of digital entertainment.

notes.title: Rise of the Triad news is coming soon
notes.notes:
Whole months worth of my teenagehood were lost to the original Rise of the Triad, and the 2013 reboot wasn't too shabby either. So it's exciting that something Rise of the Triad related is being teased. I'd speculate that it's a sequel, but that's just a guess.

The tease comes via the official Rise of the Triad Twitter account, which tweeted the above image, a link to a YouTube video, as well as the text "soon" and "please stand by... your bazookas". The video is embedded below, and features the above image soundtracked by what I'm guessing is music from the forthcoming game. 

It's a good time for a new Rise of the Triad: fast-paced, twitch-oriented shooters are definitely making a comeback, especially with a new Doom looming on the horizon. The more of these games the better, if you ask me. Running and gunning for life.

notes.title: One Year Anniversary! Workshop Done! More to Come! TL:DR We
notes.notes:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/ATZxDbP.jpg[/img]
[b]Hey everyone.[/b] Strap yourselves in, because this is going to be a LONG one. Or maybe not. Who knows, I'm making it up as I go along [b]AS USUAL.[/b]
[quote]NOW, before I get all nostalgic on you, know a few things. SteamWorks and Workshop testing are pretty much done! It's coming SOON. So are NEW updates with NEW content and tweaks and fixes and changes and THE SOUNDTRACK with NEW SONGS. We're even prepping a whole NEW EDITION of the game. It's all in the works. GET HYPE. But now, back to the nostalgia...[/quote]
One year ago we put out this here reboot of [i]Rise of the Triad[/i]. We wanted to make a game that was insanely faithful to the original ROTT, specificlly for fans of the original ROTT and old school FPS fans in general. We thought we were making a small game for a small audience. 

[b]WE WERE WRONG.[/b]

Since revealing this thing back at Quake Con 2012, old school shooter fans, Apogee/3DRealms fans and ROTT fans have been coming out of the woodwork, and somehow you all seemed to end up right here. With us. Playing our crazy culty reboot of a crazy culty game - week in and week out - for over a year since release. [b]Crazy, innit?[/b] ːKoinː

[img]http://popcultureblog.dallasnews.com/files/2013/07/2013-07-27_00014.jpg[/img]

And it's done [b]a lot[/b] for all of us involved. [b]Interceptor Entertainment[/b], once a mod team, is now a fully realized game development studio in Denmark. Fresch and the guys are busy working on a new game called [i]Bombshell[/i] (and still working on ROTT of course). And if you hadn't heard, they also acquired 3DRealms. No really. Interceptor [b]owns[/b] 3DRealms now. Wild. Almost as wild as Fred's hair. ːclaughː

The team members who didn't stay with IE after ROTT have mostly gone on to work at bigger studios such as [b]IO Interactive, Cryptic, Wargaming, The Creative Assembly[/b] and more. It's pretty wild. Have I said that enough yet? Well, this whole thing has been pretty wild, [b]MAN.[/b]

I even started my own small company with some friends (hi [b]Aaron[/b]) called [b]New Blood Interactive.[/b] We're making games, art, music, all sorts of nonsense. We also just helped put out [i]The Red Solstice[/i] on Steam. GO CHECK IT OUT.

And [b]Apogee?[/b] They're [i]BACK IN ACTION[/i]. Hard at work publishing more ROTT content, re-releasing old gems from the back catalog - and even working on some super top secret projects you're probably going to love. I think we can all agree the world is a better place with the Apogee logo in it. [b]YEAH IT IS.[/b]
http://youtu.be/F1ZO7Qxvpc8
But we couldn't of gotten here without [b]YOU[/b]. Everyone who has been here with us since day one. Everyone who bought the game. Everyone who loved the game. Hell, even everyone who hated the game. You have all helped us to become better game developers, artists, coders, animators, marketers, admins, musicians, sound engineers, forum mods, community managers, PR people, and just better people in general.

Your feedback, your involvement, your countless hours of playing over the past year have shaped us all into better people - and for that we are eternally thankful. Have some porridge. It's on the house. ːPorridgeː

[b]BUT SOME OF YOU DESERVE MORE THANKS THAN OTHERS.[/b]

After ROTT '13 came out we were a small team faced with a bigger game launch than we ever could have anticipated. The game still needed work, and we needed help. Some of you stepped up in a BIG way. And still do to this day.

So to the ROTT community mod/testing/whatever team: [b]Shadow, Hackman, Andy, Gingy, Lain, Jefe, Earth, Avain, Callahan, Cannibal, Tempus, Riet and even Lotica.[/b] Not to forget our actual factual QA lead [b]James[/b], [b]Terry[/b] from Apogee, herr [b]Fresch[/b], Level Lord [b]Leon[/b], Art God [b]Chris[/b] (topher from England), Shredmaster [b]Andrew[/b] and of course our based polski programmer: [b]Grzegorz[/b] (and the new guy [b]Aleksandr[/b]). [b]THANK YOU.[/b] For keeping ROTT alive. For keeping the community involved. And for continuing to make the game better every day. ːTriadː

Our community may be small, but everyone knows we're insanely active, and just pretty insane in general. You only have to show up to Saturday Night ROTT once to figure that out. ːGibː

And speaking of SNR. To that [b]Gijz[/b] guy - thanks for making all these dumb videos. We love them. Never stop. Ever. No really. DON'T EVER STOP: https://www.youtube.com/user/Gijzzzzzzz

http://youtu.be/U5wgrC8CyNY
http://youtu.be/h7WBVmvs-hM
http://youtu.be/kjRlDLB8w8Y
http://youtu.be/grJIMM-U9Ek
http://youtu.be/R7Gmr4ci8dQ
http://youtu.be/s4fHH128XN0
http://youtu.be/MtVxkBnt-t0
http://youtu.be/-oKa_HJJvn0
http://youtu.be/DgYXXiEp_cg
Ahh, such memories...

You know, I was hanging out drinking with Tom Hall one time and he said something to me that I've come to realize is very, very true. 

I was telling him about [i]Rise of the Triad[/i] fans. I was trying to describe you guys. But I couldn't quite put it into words. I said, "You know, ROTT fans... they're... they're..."

But before I could think of the word he stopped me there and said... [b]"Kinda weird about it?!"[/b]

[b]YEAH. KINDA WEIRD ABOUT IT.[/b] 

So here's to you! 
Here's to us!
[b]To the werid ones![/b]

And to ROTT.

May the gibs always be plentiful and may they always be [b]LUDICROUS[/b]

ːAnkhː

notes.title: ROTT v1.2 is coming SOON - Here's What's In It!
notes.notes:
Hey guys, we've been hard at work on v1.2 and it should be out SOON. Like actually SOON not usual SOON. Meanwhile, I figured I'd let you know what's coming in the update, so you can prepare and hopfully share my corny marketing copy with your friends and family!

Rise of the Triad v1.2 is here and with it come some of the most requested fan features!

[b]The Ludicrous Development Kit![/b]

      Create your own custom maps and mods with over 16,000 ROTTen assets including the complete set of assets imported from the original classic so you can party like it's 1995!
Check out the previously released video of the Classic Editor Mode on YouTube: http://youtu.be/WNOsfV7cCyk
[b]Quicksaves![/b]

      The most requested feature by the community allows players to now save and load their game anywhere at anytime! Try not to use it TOO often: http://i.imgur.com/B68eYHC.jpg http://i.imgur.com/o31s6jD.jpg

[b]No More Loggins, Kenny![/b]

      Forgot your username? Forgot your password? Who cares! With ROTT 1.2 you will only need to login to our servers if you want to sync your offline saves, post your high scores to the leaderboards or chat with other players via our in-game chat rooms. Logging in is no longer required for multiplayer at all! Now nothing gets in the way of you and your game - not even a few simple mouse clicks and keystrokes!

[b]Dozens of new fixes, tweaks, changes and optimizations![/b] 

      There are simply too many to list here, but you can read all about them on our forums: [insert forum link which doesn't exist yet here]

Pre-Purchase Now - Rise of the Triad
notes.notes:
Pre-Purchase Rise of the Triad Now and get the Apogee Throwback Pack, which includes the original Rise of the Triad, for Free!

Apogee Software and Interceptor Entertainment proudly present the rebirth of the cult-classic first-person shooter, “Rise of the Triad”. Bigger, better and more ludicrous than ever before. The H.U.N.T returns with a full single-player campaign, a fully featured multiplayer experience and so much more.

-Step into the shoes of the H.U.N.T. (High-Risk United Nations Taskforce) with five unique characters, each with different play styles
-Blast through over 20 of levels of explosive single-player action
-Unique multiplayer maps bring back all the fun and excitement of classic ROTT
-The full arsenal of over-the top weapons is back, including the Flamewall, Firebomb, Split Missile, Drunk Missile and, of course, the Excalibat!
-The maniacal modes return, with God mode, Elasto mode, Mercury mode, Shrooms mode and everyone's favorite, Dog mode!
-Build your own levels, mods and share them SOON™ with Valve's Steam Workshop
-Offline single-player and multiplayer allows for instant action
-Find tons of secrets, collectables, special events and hidden areas to explore
-Get more than 100 achievements to add to your score, which is tracked on our worldwide leaderboard and stat-tracking system
-ROTT is bloodier and more ludicrous than ever, with full character and enemy dismemberment
-The iconic original soundtrack has been completely re-forged in the fires of heavy metal!
-Nostalgia abounds with the option to play with all the original sounds and music

notes.title: Now Available - The Apogee Throwback Pack
notes.notes:
The Apogee Throwback Pack is Now Available on Steam. In addition, if you pre-purchase Rise of the Triad on Steam you will get The Apogee Throwback Pack for Free!

The Apogee Throwback Pack is a collection of four classic Apogee Software titles all in one kick ass package. Blast your way across the galaxy as British Special Agent Blake Stone in "Aliens of Gold" and "Planet Strike", then take on an ancient evil menace as the H.U.N.T in "Rise of the Triad".

Four classic games that offer hours and hours of nostalgia ridden gameplay. Full widescreen support for modern Windows and Mac operating systems. All wrapped up in one sleek package that allows for easy modding.

- Blake Stone: Aliens of Gold
- Blake Stone: Planet Strike
- Rise of the Triad
- Extreme Rise of the Triad
